content:
You draft referral notes that a primary care provider (PCP) sends to a specialist. The PCP will review, edit and sign your draft, so write it in the PCP's voice, ready to send.

The reader is a specialist who has never met this patient and is triaging many referrals. They need to know quickly why the patient is being sent now, what question the PCP wants answered, what has already been tried or worked up, and anything that would change how they manage the patient. Lead with that. Leave out chart content this specialist has no use for.

Your source is a structured chart extract plus whatever the PCP typed, including their answers to follow-up questions. Every clinical statement in the note must come from one of those. The extract has no free-text notes, so symptoms, examination findings, functional status and patient preferences are absent unless the PCP supplied them; do not supply them yourself. When something this specialist would expect is missing, a follow-up question was left unanswered, or two entries in the chart disagree, say so in the final section so the PCP can fill it in before sending. A note that reads complete but contains an invented detail is worse than one with a visible gap.

Give dates for results and events. For a trend, state the direction with the first and latest values and their dates rather than listing every reading.

Format: plain text with no markdown, because the draft goes into an editable text field. Put each section heading in capitals on its own line, in this order:

REASON FOR REFERRAL
CLINICAL QUESTION
RELEVANT HISTORY
CURRENT MEDICATIONS AND ALLERGIES
KEY RESULTS
WORKUP AND TREATMENT TO DATE
OTHER RELEVANT CONDITIONS
TO CONFIRM BEFORE SENDING

If the PCP gave no clinical question, propose the one the data best supports and mark it "[suggested - confirm]". Aim for one page, roughly 250 to 400 words. Start directly with the first heading; do not add a greeting, sign-off or commentary about the draft.

<referral_request>
Referring to: Cardiology
Referral condition: Ischemic heart disease / chronic heart failure
Urgency: urgent
PCP's clinical question: (none given)
PCP's additional notes: Reason for referral now: worsening breathlessness over two weeks, now breathless after walking across a room, with new swelling of both ankles. She is sleeping on three pillows.
</referral_request>

<what_this_specialist_needs>
The cardiologist will want: the cardiac diagnoses with dates, prior events and interventions (MI, PCI, CABG, heart failure admissions), latest ejection fraction and cardiac imaging, current cardiac medications (antiplatelet, statin, beta blocker, ACE inhibitor/ARB, diuretic) and obvious gaps in them, blood pressure and heart rate, lipid and glycemic control, renal function and potassium, recent emergency or inpatient encounters, and smoking status.
</what_this_specialist_needs>

Write the referral note.

REASON FOR REFERRAL
Urgent review for worsening heart failure in an 85-year-old woman with ischemic heart disease (CABG 2009-08-30) and chronic congestive heart failure (recorded 2025-04-27). Over the past two weeks she has become more breathless, now after walking across a room. She has new swelling of both ankles and is sleeping on three pillows.

CLINICAL QUESTION
[suggested - confirm] Is she decompensating, and what changes to diuretic and heart failure therapy are appropriate given her low blood pressure, renal function and potassium?

RELEVANT HISTORY
- Ischemic heart disease from 2009-08-17. CABG 2009-08-30. No MI or PCI recorded.
- Chronic congestive heart failure from 2025-04-27. LVEF 39.2% on echo 2025-05-26. No later echo in the record.
- ICU admission for heart failure 2025-11-22 via emergency department. IV furosemide 2025-11-22 to 2025-12-06.
- Heart failure hospice admission recorded 2026-07-06. Heart failure telemedicine visits continue, most recently 2026-11-16.
- Type 2 diabetes since 2004, with proliferative retinopathy (anti-VEGF injections, last 2026-09-28), neuropathy, and CKD.
- Never smoked.

CURRENT MEDICATIONS AND ALLERGIES
- Carvedilol 25 mg tablet; metoprolol succinate ER 100 mg tablet
- Losartan 50 mg tablet
- Furosemide 40 mg oral tablet
- Clopidogrel 75 mg tablet
- Simvastatin 20 mg tablet
- Nitroglycerin 0.4 mg mucosal spray
- Metformin ER 500 mg tablet
- Alendronic acid 10 mg tablet
- No allergies recorded.
- No aspirin, SGLT2 inhibitor or mineralocorticoid antagonist recorded.

KEY RESULTS
- NT-proBNP 1963.1 pg/mL (2025-04-27), 1584.4 (2025-12-06). Peak 1869.2 (2025-12-02), nadir 307 (2025-12-04).
- hs-troponin I 0 pg/mL on all 16 readings, latest 2025-12-06.
- BP 85/46 on 2026-11-16 (83/47 on 2026-11-09). Systolic was 108 in 2017. Heart rate 61 on 2026-11-09.
- eGFR 36.2 and creatinine 1.4 mg/dL on 2026-11-09. eGFR was 30.5 on 2026-06-29.
- Potassium 4.5 mmol/L on 2026-11-09 (2026 range 4.0 to 5.2). Sodium 141.3.
- Hemoglobin 12.2 g/dL on 2025-12-06.
- LDL 96.3 mg/dL on 2026-11-09 (2026 range 85.1 to 144.8). HDL 61.2. Triglycerides 139.5. Total cholesterol 185.4.
- HbA1c 5.4% on 2026-11-09, unchanged since 2026-03-16.
- Weight 77.6 kg and BMI 27.5 kg/m2 on 2026-11-09.

WORKUP AND TREATMENT TO DATE
- Cardiovascular stress test and NYHA assessment 2025-04-27. ECGs 2025-04-27 to 2025-11-22. Chest imaging 2025-11-22. Report text not in the extract.
- Heart failure education 2025-12-07.
- Furosemide injection stopped 2025-12-06. Oral furosemide, carvedilol and losartan are recorded as started 2026-11-09.
- Eleven urgent care visits in the past 24 months, most recent 2026-10-12.

OTHER RELEVANT CONDITIONS
- Anemia (since 2004). Osteoporosis. Microalbuminuria (2026-01-12).

TO CONFIRM BEFORE SENDING
- No symptoms, examination, current NYHA class, fluid status or today's vitals. Please add these, plus whether she has had any ED visit since 2026-11-16.
- Hospice admission on 2026-07-06 conflicts with ongoing outpatient visits. Confirm whether hospice is active and her goals of care.
- SpO2 79% on every reading 2025-12-01 to 2025-12-06. Confirm this is accurate.
- Weight is 77.6 kg at every 2026 reading. Confirm current weight.
- Creatinine 1.8 with eGFR 62.5 on 2026-10-19 do not match. CKD is listed as stage 2, but eGFR 36.2 is in the stage 3b range. Confirm.
- Carvedilol 25 mg and metoprolol succinate 100 mg are both active. Confirm which beta-blocker is intended.
- Confirm whether losartan and furosemide are still appropriate with SBP 85.
- Metformin with eGFR 36. Confirm dose.
- Confirm whether simvastatin 20 mg is intended given LDL 96.3 after CABG.
- Confirm whether the absence of aspirin, SGLT2 inhibitor and MRA is deliberate.
- The chart lists "BMI 30+ obesity" but recorded BMI is 27.5. Confirm.
- Medication review is flagged as due.
